full_judgment: 4. Both the trial Court and the lower appellate Court in decreeing the suit held that in answer to the Board's letter dated 1.2.94 asking for explanation, the Head Examiner by a letter dated 9.2.94 stated that he marked question-answer Nos. 5 and 7 in English II paper script as "1" and "9" respectively before he sent the mark sheet and his report to the Board, but inadvertently did not so mention in the report and mark sheet. When the respondent's answer scripts were scrutinized upon his application for scrutiny the re-Examiner submitted a report stating that the Head Examiner had increased the marks after submitting the report and mark sheet. The Head Examiner by his reply dated 5.12.93 denied the allegations made by the re-Examiner. By deliberately withholding the said reply of the Head Examiner dated 5.12.93 an adverse presumption was drawn against the petitioner. Both the Courts below found that the Head Examiner added 2 marks to the concerned scripts before sending his report and the mark sheet. After adding a general grace of 10 marks given by the Board, the respondent had passed the examination.
